findings.explanation: backfill_all {} is unconditional: every consumer of this module triggers a full historical backfill of the entire replicated database when the stream is created, and again whenever it is recreated. On a large production MySQL source that is a sustained read load the caller cannot opt out of, throttle, or scope. The provider supports backfill_none {} and backfill_all { mysql_excluded_objects { ... } }, neither of which is reachable here.
findings.remediation: Add var.backfill_strategy ("all"|"none", default "all") selected with dynamic blocks, plus an optional var.backfill_excluded_databases feeding mysql_excluded_objects.
findings.title: Stream hardcodes backfill_all with no way to disable or exclude objects

findings.explanation: max_concurrent_cdc_tasks and max_concurrent_backfill_tasks are unset, so Datastream chooses its own parallelism against the source database. Combined with the unconditional backfill in HOLDEN_BP_001, an operator has no lever to reduce load on a MySQL primary that is also serving application traffic.
findings.remediation: Expose var.max_concurrent_cdc_tasks and var.max_concurrent_backfill_tasks (nullable numbers, default null) and set them on mysql_source_config.
findings.title: mysql_source_config sets no concurrency limits for CDC or backfill tasks

findings.explanation: With source_hierarchy_datasets and no dataset_id_prefix, Datastream names each destination BigQuery dataset after the source schema alone. Two streams in the same project replicating source databases that share a schema name both target the same dataset, silently interleaving two sources' tables. The module already namespaces its connection profiles and private connection with var.stream_id; the destination is the only unnamespaced surface.
findings.remediation: Add dataset_id_prefix to dataset_template, defaulting to a sanitised var.stream_id.
findings.title: source_hierarchy_datasets dataset_template has no dataset_id_prefix

findings.explanation: var.source_database is a single string wired into one static mysql_databases block, so replicating a second database or restricting to specific tables requires editing the module rather than passing a variable. Consumers hit this immediately on any multi-schema MySQL instance.
findings.remediation: Change var.source_database to list(string) (or a map of database -> tables) and generate mysql_databases with a dynamic block.
findings.title: include_objects is fixed to exactly one database with no table-level scoping

findings.explanation: All four Datastream resources support labels, but only google_datastream_stream.main receives var.labels. Cost-allocation and ownership queries over the module's resources return a partial picture, and the inconsistency is invisible to a caller reading only variables.tf.
findings.remediation: Add labels = var.labels to both connection profiles and the private connection.
findings.title: var.labels is applied only to the stream, not to the connection profiles or private connection

findings.explanation: None of the four resources set project, so the module can only deploy into whatever project the ambient google provider resolves. A root config managing several projects must define an aliased provider per project and pass it in, rather than varying an input.
findings.remediation: Add variable "project" { type = string, default = null } and set project = var.project on all four resources; null preserves today's provider-inherited behaviour.
findings.title: No project variable; every resource inherits the provider's default project

findings.explanation: Fixing BP_001/002/004/006 added six inputs, crossing HLD_TF_027 threshold of 15. Each knob is justified individually but the flat surface is now large.
findings.remediation: Grouped into three object-typed variables: source_mysql {hostname, port, username, password}, backfill {strategy, excluded_databases}, max_concurrent_tasks {cdc, backfill}. 19 inputs -> 14; HLD_TF_027 clears.
findings.title: Module input surface grew to 19 variables

suggested_policies.rationale: A Datastream stream writing to BigQuery via source_hierarchy_datasets with no dataset_id_prefix names destination datasets after the source schema alone, so two streams replicating same-named schemas collide into one dataset. Single unambiguous attribute path on one resource type; fires correctly on any config using source_hierarchy_datasets.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX  # run: holden next-id --cloud GCP
name: Datastream BigQuery hierarchy datasets should set a dataset_id_prefix
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  With source_hierarchy_datasets and no dataset_id_prefix, Datastream derives each
  destination BigQuery dataset name from the source schema name alone. Two streams
  in the same project whose sources share a schema name write into the same dataset,
  interleaving unrelated tables and making the destination ambiguous.
remediation: |
  Set a prefix that namespaces the stream:
    source_hierarchy_datasets {
      dataset_template {
        location          = var.location
        dataset_id_prefix = var.stream_id
      }
    }
resources:
  google_datastream_stream:
    path: destination_config.bigquery_destination_config.source_hierarchy_datasets.dataset_template.dataset_id_prefix
    not_null: true
